name: Hirect Ltd
title: Hirect Ltd - 504036 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Hirect Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.3% to INR258.4 crore, but EBITDA fell 45.4% YoY to INR13.2 crore as Elventive France drags margins.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 20.3% to INR258.4 crore, while consolidated EBITDA of INR13.2 crore fell 45.4% YoY (up 57% QoQ), with margin of 5.1% after the call's correction. Standalone revenue grew 10.1% to INR236.4 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 3.2% to INR25.1 crore at a 10.6% margin. Management described flat order intake for the quarter, citing delayed government tender finalisations, and said the company still targets 30% growth for the year. Management expects Elventive France margin drag to persist for another 3 to 5 quarters before breakeven.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before exceptional item and tax
financial_highlights.change: Significant sequential improvement; YoY not stated

financial_highlights.value: INR9.4 crore, including INR3.5 crore exceptional gain from sale of Dehradun plant

financial_highlights.change: +7.2% YoY; margin moderated on raw material costs tied to West Asia crisis

segments.name: Standalone India (Hirect business)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR236.4 crore (+10.1% YoY), EBITDA margin 10.6%, gross margin 25.5%. Copper conductor division saved about 2% of material cost; management said the benefit is in its infancy.

segments.name: Elventive France
segments.commentary: Drags consolidated margin through integration and scale-up costs (higher employee and operating expenses). Management expects 3 to 5 quarters before breakeven; restructuring measures under consideration; in talks with German automakers.

segments.name: Hirect Global / exports
segments.commentary: First US order for traction motor assemblies, delivery within the year. US order for IGBT converters for mining: initial prototype orders, expected to ship within about 6 months, with bulk orders possible after commissioning.

segments.name: New businesses: MEMU and Vande Metro
segments.commentary: First MEMU trainset development order from Modern Coach Factory worth about INR60 crore (4 trainsets, integrated propulsion system). First order in the first-ever Vande Metro tender, covering design, development and commissioning.

segments.name: Copper conductors
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 350 metric tonnes: about 220 MT CTC (expandable) and the rest PICC/EPICC. Focus this year is internal consumption for transformers; external orders mainly in the power sector are being sought.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a target of 30% growth for the year, saying flat Q1 order intake does not change it.
Long-term ambition of becoming a INR1 billion revenue company in about 5 years; management said the strategy is already in play but will not be made public.
Elventive France to take 3 to 5 quarters more of margin pressure before breakeven; CFO confirmed EBITDA breakeven in 4 to 5 quarters.

Several tenders where Hirect is L1, L2 or L3 are expected to be finalised soon, with some propulsion tenders possibly finalised by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026 per call timing, stated as 'this quarter').
Management declined to quantify delayed orders, FY27 closing order book, or margin profile by product.
capex_capacity: Satpur facility: traction transformer capacity raised 20%, from 60 to nearly 75 transformers per month.
Locomotive propulsion system capacity of about 120 sets per annum; facility being staged for further volumes, with production not seen as a constraint.
Sinnar facility covers propulsion systems, battery chargers, traction motors, HVAC systems and the copper conductor plant.
R&D: more than 200 engineers across Mumbai (core technology) and Hyderabad (software and digital intelligence); more than 50 products under active development.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake described as flattish; management attributed the delay to geopolitical factors causing temporary government policy pivots.

Indigenous propulsion platform: field trials at about 9,000 to 10,000 km, delayed by Gujarat floods; now a UVAM development source eligible for 20% of tender quantities, with about 6 to 7 approved sources competing for the other 80%.
Content per platform: about INR5.5 crore per locomotive, about INR15 crore per MEMU trainset, about INR60 crore per Vande Metro trainset. MEMU tenders run about 200 to 250 trainsets a year.
Electronics component shortages in the industry are causing lopsided inventory at customers; management said Hirect has not been severely affected yet.
Payment for propulsion systems is received after delivery, not on milestones, per the call. Delivery cycle cited at about 18 to 20 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the copper conductor capacity split between CTC and enamelled/paper-insulated conductors, and what revenue share is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the 350 MT installed, about 220 MT is CTC (expandable) and the rest is PICC/EPICC, where EPICC capacity is above 350 MT. This year is focused on internal use, with external orders mainly in the power sector.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify delayed orders or give a closing FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either, saying positions are strong and it is a matter of time before orders are placed.

qa_highlights.question: Will consolidated EBITDA margin of about 5% fall further, or is it sustainable for 4 to 5 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone margin is about 10.8%. Consolidated margin is depressed by Elventive France, and the CFO expects 3 to 4 quarters before recovery; he confirmed Elventive reaches EBITDA breakeven in 4 to 5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAM for railway propulsion, given the 1 billion revenue aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Locomotive propulsion TAM is about 1,500 units a year, tapering to about 1,200. Management said the bigger opportunity is trainsets, and that the 1 billion ambition does not rely only on Indian Railways propulsion.

qa_highlights.question: Why stay as a development vendor rather than a main vendor for propulsion?
qa_highlights.answer: Development status gives access to 20% of tender quantities, against 80% contested by 6 to 7 approved sources; management said this is mathematically more attractive for now.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US IGBT converter opportunity and its path to scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is bound by NDA and could not give ratings or configuration. Shipment is expected within 6 months; repeat bulk orders are expected after commissioning and satisfactory performance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margins compress, and has the cost escalation clause changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said margins held up, with higher employee costs from recruitment (over 200 R&D staff) as the main drag. The escalation clause is unchanged.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin (5.1%) and EBITDA decline of 45.4% YoY; Elventive France breakeven timing of 3 to 5 quarters.
Tender finalisation delays for propulsion and MEMU/Vande Metro orders; no order book quantification given.
Electronics component shortages could affect deliveries if Hirect is affected, per management.
Raw material cost inflation linked to the West Asia crisis is compressing standalone gross margin (25.5%).
Reported 'L1/L2/L3' positions and the 30% growth target are not yet backed by booked orders in Q1; watch Q2 order inflows.
Possible tender qualification changes (for example, the technology age or local-content conditions in recent news) that management said do not apply to current products.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the trainset and US wins, but guarded on near-term numbers: management declined to quantify delayed orders, FY27 order book, or product-level margins. CFO candid that consolidated margins will stay under pressure for 3 to 5 quarters because of Elventive France.
key_quotes: Had it not been for the copper division, our gross margins would have been adversely affected by about 2%.
Our target for the year of achieving 30% growth stays intact and the year so far has only strengthened our ambition.
So mathematically, it makes a little bit more sense to be where we are at this stage.

adds.what: Satpur traction transformer capacity raised 20%, from 60 to nearly 75 transformers per month

growth.why: Management reiterated 30% FY27 revenue growth despite flat Q1 order intake, backed by a MEMU order (~INR60 crore), a first Vande Metro order, US export orders and a 20% Satpur transformer capacity increase, but tender finalisations are delayed and the company declined to quantify the order book.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin is 5.1% (down from a higher base, EBITDA -45.4% YoY) and management expects Elventive France drag for 3-5 more quarters before breakeven; standalone gross margin fell to 25.5% on West Asia raw material costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Satpur traction transformer capacity already raised 20% (60 to ~75 per month) and locomotive propulsion capacity of ~120 sets per year is being staged for further volumes, so further adds are guided but not sized.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates 30% FY27 growth target, but Q1 order intake was flat and tender finalisations are delayed; standalone revenue grew only 10.1% YoY to INR236.4 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; the 20% transformer capacity add is already commissioned and no new capex is guided, so a fresh announcement depends on MEMU/Vande Metro and propulsion tender wins.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 30% growth target but explicitly tied it to tender finalisations that have not yet converted into booked orders; flat Q1 order intake argues against an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Flat Q1 order intake, delayed government tenders and unquantified order book leave the 30% growth target exposed; Elventive breakeven is 4-5 quarters away.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: US traction motor assemblies and IGBT converter for mining expected to ship within about 6 months, and MEMU trainset (INR60 crore, 4 trainsets) development under way; more than 50 products under active development.

rows.label: MEMU trainset order and first Vande Metro win
rows.why: First MEMU development order from Modern Coach Factory worth about INR60 crore (4 trainsets) and first Vande Metro tender order are already secured, though MEMU tenders run about 200-250 trainsets a year.

rows.label: US exports: traction motors and IGBT converters
rows.why: First US traction motor assembly order to deliver within the year and IGBT converter prototype orders to ship in about 6 months, with bulk orders possible after commissioning.

rows.label: Elventive France breakeven
rows.why: CFO confirmed EBITDA breakeven in 4-5 quarters, though consolidated margin of 5.1% stays depressed until then.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term strategy, MEMU and Vande Metro wins and US exports, but cautious on near-term numbers, declining to quantify delayed orders, the FY27 order book or product margins; analysts pushed on margin sustainability at Elventive France and the 30% growth target.
